title: TV presenter and comedian Bill Oddie dies at 85
facts: British TV presenter and comedian Bill Oddie died at the age of 85.
David Foster served as the talent agent for Bill Oddie.
Bill Oddie rose to prominence in the 1970s as a member of the television comedy trio The Goodies.
Bill Oddie served as an original presenter on the BBC television programme Springwatch.
Kate Humble co-presented the television series Springwatch alongside Bill Oddie.
Chris Packham succeeded Bill Oddie as a presenter on Springwatch.
Bill Oddie was born in Rochdale, near Manchester.
Bill Oddie attended Cambridge University and performed with the Cambridge Footlights comedy troupe.
Bill Oddie wrote for the 1960s satirical television series That Was The Week That Was.
Bill Oddie wrote the novelty songs 'The Funky Gibbon' and 'The Inbetweenies', which reached the UK top 10.
The Goodies television comedy series broadcast for 12 years beginning in 1970.
Bill Oddie was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) in 2003 for services to wildlife conservation.
Bill Oddie co-presented the first four series of Springwatch starting in 2005.
Bill Oddie previously served as a vice president of the RSPCA animal charity.
Bill Oddie was married to children's television writer and artist Laura Beaumont.
